messages:
Anika: Ran a cross-GPU attention probe this morning. L40S has a nasty tail spike at batch=64 / seqlen=2048 when paged-attn gets invoked. Posting quick logs and perf notes below.

Anika: Command I ran:
```
$ ./bench/run_attention.py --gpu L40S --model gpt-j-6b \
    --kernels flash,fused,paged \
    --seqs 128,512,1024,2048 --batches 1,8,32,64 --iters 60 \
```

Anika: Condensed results (ms per token, median / p95):
- flash: batch64 seq2048: 3.2 / 18.7
- fused: batch64 seq2048: 3.5 / 20.1
- paged: batch64 seq2048: 4.8 / 290.2  <-- huge tail

Anika: nvprof / CUPTI sampling around the spike shows repeated kernel fallback events and PCIe stalls aligned with `paged_kv_restore` kernel.
```
nvprof sample:
  paged_kv_restore: avg 120ms, p95 280ms
  kernel_fallback_event: occurred ~12x during one batch flush
  pci_bandwidth_spike aligned to those restores
```

Mike: yikes. did you capture the KV page hit/miss counters?

Anika: yes — aggregated per-run (seq2048, batch64):
- kv_page_hits: 88%
- kv_page_misses: 12%
- avg pages restored per request: 3.6
- worst-case restore latency: 240ms

Anika: pattern looks like when miss rate crosses ~10% we fall into a cascading restore loop that blocks the queue and causes p95 to blow up.

Devon: interesting — I've seen similar behavior on L40S with long sequences. H100 had a smaller effect, A100 didn't show it in our quick test. Could be PCIe and DMA concurrency limits on L40S + our current batching heuristic.

Jordy: what heuristics do we run for batching timeout?

Anika: currently we accumulate for up to 8ms or until batch-size threshold. That helps throughput but with seq=2048 the per-request restore work saturates the dma engine and we queue more batches behind it.

Devon: proposal: 2 quick mitigations:
- lower batch-accum timeout for L40S when seq > 1024 (try 2ms)
- change fallback policy: if kv_page_miss_rate > 10% then prefer fused (no paged restore) or split the batch across two GPUs instead of invoking paged restore synchronously.

Anika: I'll try an experiment toggling batch-timeout to 2ms and force-disable paged fallback for seq>=1024. Re-running now.

ci-bot: Benchmark job queued: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/bench/1765127890/results (logs + flamegraphs) :white_check_mark:

Anika: quick follow-up from the forced toggle run: p95 dropped from 290ms -> 24ms for paged-path (effectively matching fused), throughput down ~6% but tail fixed.

Mike: tradeoff seems acceptable for production — tail matters more than a small throughput hit. Can you paste the flamegraph snippet?

Anika: flamegraph (cropped):
```
- host submit
  - batch_assemble
  - paged_kv_restore (spike)
    - page_read
    - dma_wait
  - attention_kernel
```

Jordy: good call. I'll add a quick runtime flag `--force-paged-disable-threshold=0.10` and a device profile for L40S. We should also add a perf regression alert that triggers if p95 increases >3x vs baseline for any kernel.

Devon: note — we should sanity-check on H100/A100 before flipping in Dedicated. H100 had a mild bump; might be safe to keep paged on H100.

Anika: filing a perf ticket with reproducer + logs. Tagging @eng-runtime to review the heuristic patch: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4219 (linked logs & ci run).

Mike: thanks — great reproducible notes. Once patch is up we can run cross-region Dedicated perf tests. :+1:

Anika: I'll follow up with a tiny RFC for the heuristic change (short lived toggle + metrics) and a rollout plan.
